Whey protein is rich in essential amino acids and branched-chain amino acids, have biological activities (Zhang, Ding, & Li, 2021), such as promote the chelation of metal ions (Sun et al., 2017), antioxidant (Hernández-Ledesma et al., 2005), antibacterial (Théolier et al., 2013). Consequently, whey protein can be used as an optimal raw material for the preparation of whey protein iron chelating peptides and whey protein peptide-iron chelate (WPP-Fe). The aim of this research was to utilize whey protein as a raw material for producing iron-chelating peptides and to evaluate the whey protein peptides-iron chelate (WPP-Fe) from structure, morphology, stability, bacteriostatic properties and DPPH radical scavenging ability.
The whey protein peptides-iron chelate had good pH, salt concentration and gastrointestinal digestive stability compared to FeCl2, ferrous gluconate and ferrous glycine. Besides, the DPPH eliminate ability and bacteriostatic properties of the whey protein peptides-iron chelate (WPP-Fe) were better than the whey protein peptide (WPP). These findings can be used as a theoretical basis for the development of new peptide iron supplements.
To improve its utilization in the food industry, this study investigated the identification, virtual screening, and mechanisms of angiotensin-I-converting enzyme (ACE)-inhibitory peptides with antioxidant and ferrous-chelating abilities from Ginkgo kernel glutelin-2 hydrolysates via intergrade in vitro and in silico methods.
In this study, the WPP-Fe chelate was successfully prepared with whey protein iron chelating peptides, and the chelating rate and chelating yield was 85.92% and 77.70%, respectively. The WPP formed stable chelates with ferrous ions through amino, carboxyl and imidazole groups.
